original_question: Assume F is a foliation of geometric degree d ≥ 2 on P2, the line at infinity is invariant, and all singularities are hyperbolic. Do all non-compact leaves of F, meaning all leaves except the compact curves, admit Green functions?
target_in_paper: Section 6, Problem 6.1(i): Assume that F is a foliation of geometric degree d on P^2 with the line at infinity invariant and having only hyperbolic singularities. Do the leaves, except for the compact curves, have Green functions?
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's actual target very closely: it is about a foliation of geometric degree d on P^2, with invariant line at infinity and only hyperbolic singularities, and it asks whether every leaf other than the compact ones admits Green functions. That is exactly the scope of Problem 6.1(i), not the broader Problem 6.1(ii).
missing_details: The paper is working over the complex numbers: the ambient space is the complex projective plane P^2(C).
The object is a holomorphic foliation by Riemann surfaces, not an arbitrary topological or smooth foliation.
The degree is the geometric degree of the foliation; the paper does not impose the extra restriction d >= 2.
The excluded leaves are described in the paper as the compact curves, i.e. compact invariant curves or compact leaves supported by compact curves.
The singularities being hyperbolic means that at each singular point, the quotient of the eigenvalues of a linearized local vector field is non-real.
The Green-function question is leafwise: each individual noncompact leaf is viewed as a Riemann surface and asked to admit a Green function.
The line at infinity should be understood as the distinguished projective line L_infty in an affine chart of P^2.
refined_question: Let F be a holomorphic foliation by Riemann surfaces of geometric degree d on the complex projective plane P^2(C). Assume that the line at infinity L_infty is F-invariant and that every singularity of F is hyperbolic, meaning that at each singular point the quotient of the eigenvalues of a linearized local vector field defining F is non-real. Must every leaf of F that is not a compact invariant curve admit a Green function?
justification: The draft is essentially a near-verbatim restatement of Section 6, Problem 6.1(i). The nearby context in Section 6 explains why this is the precise open case: Brunella's result covers foliations with no leaf supported by a compact curve, while the authors also recall that when compact curves are present and the singularities are hyperbolic, the directed dd^c-closed currents are exactly the integration currents on those compact curves. This leaves the function theory of the remaining leaves as the question asked in Problem 6.1(i). The introductory sections also define geometric degree and explain the meaning of hyperbolic singularities. Your only substantive deviation from the paper is the added hypothesis d >= 2, which the paper does not require.
